name: Deep Analysis
oracle_text:
Target player draws two cards.
Flashback—{1}{U}, Pay 3 life. (You may cast this card from your graveyard for its flashback cost. Then exile it.)
blocked_sentences: Flashback—{1}{U}, Pay 3 life. (You may cast this card from your graveyard for its flashback cost. Then exile it.)

needs.what: A card-level `flashback` field carrying a full alternative cost (mana `{1}{U}` plus `pay_life: 3`) that legality offers only for a copy of the card in its owner's graveyard, replacing the printed mana cost rather than adding to it
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `retrace` is the only field that widens legality to scan the graveyard (legality._cast_actions loops `state.players[pid].graveyard` on `card.retrace`), but it is a bare boolean: `CardDef.retrace_cost` is hardcoded to `Cost(discard=1, discard_selector={'types': ['Land']})` and `game.py` charges it *in addition* to the printed `{3}{U}`, so it can express neither a cheaper alternative mana cost nor a life payment as part of the alternative cost. `kicker` is a string cost but is an additional cost paid from the hand and never changes which zone a card may be cast from. `suspend` names an alternative cost but plays the card from exile after a counter countdown, not from the graveyard on demand. Cycling -- newly shipped as `Cost.discard_self` plus `active_zones` on an activated ability -- is the closest new arrival and is still the wrong shape twice over: it *activates* an ability rather than *casting* the card, so the spell never goes on the stack and `spell_effects` never run and the draw would have to be duplicated into the ability; and loader.py:326 requires any ability active outside the battlefield to pay `discard_self`, i.e. to remove its source from that zone by discarding, which a graveyard card cannot do. Cost already carries `pay_life`, so the life half exists; what is missing is any way to attach a whole alternative cost to a graveyard *cast*.

needs.what: A once-only rider on that alternative cast: when the spell resolves (or is countered) it goes to exile instead of the graveyard, so the card cannot be flashed back a second time
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `retrace` deliberately returns the card to the graveyard and is reusable every turn, which is the opposite of flashback's once-only exile. Nothing else can substitute: the `replacements` whitelist is only `self_enters`, `self_enters_tapped` and `self_enters_with_counters`, so no card can replace a spell's move to the graveyard; and the `exile` op in `spell_effects` cannot stand in for it, because it would run on every cast including the first from hand, exiling the card before it could ever be flashed back.
